long_biography.plain_text:
By the start of the century, Al Rajhi sat on Saudi Cement's board. He later became independent chairman, a non-executive governance position distinct from the company's chief executive. His other public-facing work extended outside Saudi Arabia. As head of Al Rajhi Investment Group, he represented a plan to develop two Jordanian cement plants, and he subsequently chaired the group's Jordan cement subsidiary.

His development work also included leading RADIC, which contracted to build homes and infrastructure in Oman. Together, these appointments point to a career managing capital-intensive industrial and property ventures across the Gulf and Jordan. They do not, however, identify a personally held stake or explain the acquisition of his fortune. The Jordan cement business belonged to a holding company, and Saudi Cement classified his chairmanship as independent. Plant budgets, sukuk proceeds and contract totals remained company-level figures. With no disclosed inheritance allocation, founder equity, direct shareholding or recent operating platform, his wealth mechanism and present primary sector cannot be classified reliably.
